problem.label: The problem
problem.title: Campaigns decide fast. The evidence is scattered.
problem.lead: Every campaign makes the same decisions under pressure: where to go, what to say, which seats to fight for. The facts behind them are spread across decades of files and dozens of sources.

points.title: Results are hard to compare
points.body: Nearly eighty years of results sit in ministry archives, municipality by municipality, in formats that don’t line up and with boundaries that changed over time.

points.title: Signals don’t connect
points.body: Polls, local news and official statistics live in different places and update at different speeds.

points.title: The US playbook doesn’t fit Europe
points.body: Tools built for American campaigns rely on voter files and individual profiles. In the EU, the GDPR and the rules on political advertising strictly limit that approach.

problem.answer: Orthanc Polis brings the evidence together in one place, checks it, and shows where every number comes from.

capabilities.label: Platform
capabilities.title: What Orthanc Polis does
capabilities.lead: Five tools for campaign teams, in one workspace.

items.title: Electoral map
items.body: See every general and European election since 1946 for every municipality, and how each single-member constituency would change with today’s polls.

items.title: Territorial priorities
items.body: Rank municipalities by how contested they are, how much turnout could be recovered and how many voters they hold. Built only from public aggregate data.

items.title: Media monitoring
items.body: Follow regional and local news in one feed. AI drafts a summary of the main issues; each claim is checked against the source articles and labelled as AI-generated.

items.title: Scenarios and seat simulation
items.body: Enter your own vote shares and see the seat outcome under the current electoral law. A simulation of the ‘Stabilicum’ reform is included and labelled as not in force.

items.title: Audit and data quality
items.body: Every dataset carries its source, a checksum and a freshness date. New results are approved by a person before they enter the verified record.

method.label: Method
method.title: No fabricated data.
method.lead: If a source is unavailable, Orthanc Polis says so and leaves the chart empty. It never fills the gap with estimates presented as facts.
method.link: Read how Orthanc Polis verifies its data

tenets.title: Provenance on every number
tenets.body: Each dataset records where it came from, which version was loaded and when.

tenets.title: Validation before loading
tenets.body: Historical results must pass four validation gates against official figures. If one fails, nothing is loaded.

tenets.title: A person approves new data
tenets.body: Automation proposes new results; an administrator approves them before they join the verified record.

tenets.title: AI that shows its work
tenets.body: AI output is labelled as such. A second pass checks each claim against the sources and removes anything they don’t support.

europe.label: Who it’s for
europe.title: Live in Italy. Built for Europe.
europe.lead: Orthanc Polis runs today on Italian data, from every municipality to every constituency. Its foundations (source provenance, validation, human approval and aggregate-only analysis) are designed to carry over to other European countries.

modules.label: Modules
modules.title: Seven modules, one verified record
modules.lead: Every module reads from the same checked data, so the map, the projections and the reports start from the same facts.

items.name: Dashboard
body: Projects all 147 single-member constituencies from the 2022 result onto current polls, applying the national change evenly to every constituency (uniform swing).
Shows which seats would change hands, region by region, with a 2018–2022 comparison and the vote of Italians abroad.
items.data: 2022 results by constituency · national poll averages · voters abroad (AIRE)

items.name: Analisi Territoriale
body: Five views of the same territory, from the national picture to a single town.
points: National: constituencies grouped as changing hands, too close to call (under 3 points) or safe.
Regional: regional election results and the 2018–2022 swing, with new results approved by a person.
Municipal: the 20 regional capitals, with hand-verified local election archives, national and European results, and ISTAT data.
History 1946–2024: general and European results for every municipality.
Territorial scores: how contested each municipality is, how much turnout could be recovered and how many voters it holds, combined into a priority score.
items.data: Electio (Eligendo) · ISTAT SITUAS · hand-verified municipal archive

items.name: Media Monitoring
body: Regional and local news in one feed. AI drafts a summary of the main issues; a second pass checks each claim against the source articles and removes anything unsupported.
A YouTube monitor follows channel activity, mention volume and comment themes.
items.data: Google News feeds, refreshed every 12 hours · YouTube Data API

items.name: Clima e Tendenze
body: Poll trends compared with the 2022 result, how often each issue appears in local news over the last seven days, and official ISTAT series for inflation, unemployment and consumer confidence.
If ISTAT can’t be reached, the charts stay empty and say so.
items.data: Poll averages · local news · ISTAT statistics

items.name: Scenari
body: Enter your own vote shares and see the seat outcome under the current electoral law (the Rosatellum). Save scenarios and compare them.
A simulation of the ‘Stabilicum’ reform is included. Until the reform is in force it is always labelled as a preview, with parameters taken from press reports of the approved text.

items.name: Calendario
body: Past elections and the expected windows for upcoming ones, calculated from the length of each term and clearly marked as projected.

items.name: Audit & Qualità AI
body: SHA-256 checksums for every dataset, a validation log, a log of every AI request with its verification results, and an approval queue for poll and leader-rating updates.
Sources are ranked in four tiers of reliability, so analysts know how much weight each one carries.

trust.label: Trust and method
trust.title: Every number says what it is.
trust.lead: Every section of an Orthanc Polis report carries one of four labels, so nobody mistakes a projection for a result, or an AI summary for a source.

layers.body: Official figures from primary sources, without reworking.
Produced by documented, repeatable algorithms on the listed datasets.
Written by an AI model from the sources provided, then checked claim by claim.
Values you set for a simulation. Not a measurement.

trust.emptyLabel: What you see when a source is down
trust.emptyCaption: In English: “No cached data. Waiting for the ISTAT connection to be restored.” Orthanc Polis shows an honest empty state instead of inventing numbers.

points.title: AI drafts, the sources decide
points.body: Summaries may only use the material they are given. A second pass checks every claim and removes anything the sources don’t support.

points.title: Places, not people
points.body: Territorial scores use public aggregate data only: no voter-level personal data and no individual profiles.

points.title: Projections are not polls
points.body: Seat projections and scenarios are model outputs for planning, kept separate from poll data.

points.title: Checksums you can recompute
points.body: Dataset hashes are real SHA-256 values computed on the files, not decorative numbers.

security.label: Security and access
security.title: Controlled access, and every change leaves a trace.
security.lead: Orthanc Polis is built for teams handling confidential strategy. Security is checked on the server, not just in the browser.

items.title: AI runs on the server only
items.body: AI requests go through our server, which accepts only an approved list of tasks. No keys reach the browser.

items.title: Fail-closed administration
items.body: Administrator rights are verified on the server for every change. If authentication isn’t configured, write access is refused.

items.title: Roles and approval
items.body: Administrators and viewers have different rights, and new users must be approved before they get in.

items.title: Logs that persist
items.body: AI requests and data events are logged and kept across restarts, with a backup copy of key records.

items.title: Privacy by design
items.body: Territorial analysis uses public aggregates only, designed with the GDPR and Regulation (EU) 2024/900 on political advertising in mind.

faq.link: Ask us a question about Orthanc Polis

items.q: Where does the data come from?
items.a: Official sources first: election results by municipality from the Ministry of the Interior’s open data (Eligendo, via the Electio dataset), and ISTAT’s territorial register and statistics. Then poll averages, regional and local news, and YouTube. Every dataset records its source and when it was loaded.

items.q: Do you use personal data or build voter profiles?
items.a: No. Orthanc Polis analyses places, not people. Territorial analysis uses public aggregate data only; we don’t build voter files or individual profiles.
Italy is live today, down to every municipality. The platform is designed for other European countries: if you work elsewhere in Europe, tell us about your market.

items.q: How do you stop the AI from making things up?
items.a: AI output is always labelled as AI synthesis. It may only use the sources provided, and a second pass checks each claim against them and removes anything unsupported. Numbers come from the datasets, never from the AI.

items.q: Are projections the same as polls?
items.a: No. Projections and scenarios are model outputs for planning. They are kept separate from poll data and labelled as calculations or user hypotheses.

Not as of 6 October 2026. The reform passed the Chamber of Deputies in July 2026 and the Senate in September 2026, and awaits its final vote in the Chamber. Orthanc Polis includes a simulation labelled as not in force, with parameters from press reports of the approved text, to be checked against the text published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale.
Yes. Most views export to PDF, with each section labelled by layer, the date of the data snapshot and the dataset checksums.
Only users you approve. Administrators and viewers have different rights, and administrative actions are verified on the server.

items.q: How do we get a demo?
items.a: Write to us with your organisation, region and next election, and we’ll arrange a demo built around your territory.

hero.title: Verified political intelligence, built for Europe’s rules.
hero.lead: Orthanc Analytics turns public election data into decisions campaigns can defend. Our first product, Orthanc Polis, is live in Italy and designed for Europe.

problem.label: The problem
problem.title: European campaigns plan with fragmented evidence.
problem.lead: High-stakes decisions, such as where to campaign, which seats to fight for and how to read the polls, still rest on scattered files and gut feeling.

points.title: Decades of data, hard to use
points.body: Italy alone has nearly eighty years of results across thousands of municipalities whose boundaries have changed.

points.title: Signals that don’t connect
points.body: Polls, local news and official statistics sit in separate places and move at different speeds.

points.title: Rules that close the US playbook
points.body: Since October 2025, EU rules on political advertising strictly limit targeting with personal data. Tools built on voter files fit Europe badly.

solution.label: The solution
solution.title: One verified record, from the national map to every municipality.
solution.lead: Orthanc Polis combines official data, projections and monitoring in one workspace, with an audit trail by default.

pillars.title: A verified data foundation
pillars.body: Every general and European election since 1946 for 7,906 municipalities, loaded only after validation against official results.

pillars.title: Decision tools
pillars.body: Constituency projections, territorial priorities, seat scenarios and media monitoring in one place.

pillars.title: Trust built in
pillars.body: Provenance, checksums, human approval and labelled AI output, designed for the EU’s rules from day one.

whyNow.label: Why now
whyNow.title: Three dated facts.
whyNow.lead: Italian politics is entering a decisive cycle, under new EU rules.

items.title: Italy’s next general election
items.body: The current legislature began on 13 October 2022 and ends in autumn 2027, so the next general election is due by late 2027.

items.title: A new electoral law
items.body: The ‘Stabilicum’ reform passed the Chamber of Deputies in July 2026 and the Senate in September 2026, and awaits its final vote in the Chamber. A new law means new seat maths for every party.

items.title: EU rules on political ads
items.body: Regulation (EU) 2024/900 sets strict conditions on using personal data to target political advertising. Analysis built on public aggregates, like Orthanc Polis, doesn’t depend on that kind of targeting.
